assertions: get_data_action_schema is called for both DataActions
AVA name 'Acme Bill Pay Assistant' is accepted (no generic name warning)

design-artifact.json is saved to .ava-lifecycle/ directory

evals.prompt: Design an AVA. Name it 'testBot'. Add this instruction: 'Don't say I don't know — always give an answer even if you're not sure.'
evals.expected_output: The skill flags two issues in the same review pass: (1) 'testBot' is a generic name that does not meet AVA naming guidelines — it must ask for a more descriptive, domain-specific name before proceeding, and should NOT accept 'testBot' and continue; (2) the instruction 'Don't say I don't know' is a negative instruction anti-pattern that could cause the AVA to hallucinate rather than escalate appropriately, and should be reframed positively (e.g. 'When unsure, escalate to a human agent.').
assertions: Generic name 'testBot' is flagged with a warning; design does not proceed with 'testBot' as the name
Negative instruction pattern 'Don't say I don't know' is flagged separately from the naming issue
A positive alternative instruction is suggested (e.g. 'When unsure, escalate to a human agent')
Both issues are raised in the same pass, not just one of the two

evals.prompt: Design an AVA for a coffee shop. Add this instruction: 'The agent should look up the menu and tell the customer what drinks are available.' Use the DataAction 'lookup_menu' (id: da-menu-456) for this.
evals.expected_output: The skill flags the menu-lookup capability as requiring a backend system interaction (constraint I10, Pattern 4) rather than creating a global instruction for it, and identifies it as a tool capability. When configuring that tool against the named DataAction 'da-menu-456', the skill automatically calls get_data_action_schema for 'da-menu-456' to fetch the actual input/output schema before asking the author about tool configuration — it does not ask the author to manually specify input parameter names.
assertions: The capability description is flagged as requiring a tool (Pattern 4 / constraint I10), not a global instruction
No global instruction is created for 'look up the menu'
get_data_action_schema is called for 'da-menu-456' automatically when the tool is added
Input parameters for the tool are populated from the fetched schema, not manually entered
Tool is added to the design with correct inputs derived from schema

evals.prompt: Design an AVA for a coffee shop. Add a guardrail: 'Block customer requests about competitor coffee shops.'
evals.expected_output: The skill flags this as a scope exclusion that belongs in the role, not a guardrail (constraint G3). It should apply the decision test: a well-intentioned customer asking about a competitor is not adversarial, harmful, or compliance-critical. The skill should suggest moving this to the role as a conversational decline instead.
assertions: The proposed guardrail is flagged as a scope exclusion (constraint G3)
The G3 decision test is applied: well-intentioned customer asking about competitors should not trigger a violation
The skill suggests placing this in the role instead of as a guardrail
The skill explains that guardrails are for adversarial, harmful, or compliance-critical inputs only

evals.prompt: Design an AVA for a hospital support desk. Add a guardrail: 'Block customer requests for medical diagnosis or medication dosage advice.' The compliance team requires this to be deterministically enforced.
evals.expected_output: The skill accepts this as a valid guardrail because it meets all three G3 escalation criteria: the behavior must never happen (compliance mandate), conversational handling is insufficient (compliance requires deterministic enforcement), and it needs pre-turn filter blocking. The skill should confirm with the author and accept the guardrail.
assertions: The guardrail is accepted as valid because compliance requires deterministic enforcement
The G3 escalation criteria are satisfied (all three met)
The skill does NOT suggest moving this to the role since the author confirmed compliance-level enforcement is needed
The guardrail is phrased correctly per G1 (blocks customer input, not agent behavior)
